subject: literature
passage: Bilal had spent three months at his uncle's workshop in Multan, and still he had not been allowed to paint a single tile. He mixed glazes, swept up clay dust, and watched his uncle's brush trace blue vines and flowers across white surfaces. One evening, Bilal complained that he was learning nothing. His uncle said nothing; he simply handed Bilal a brush and a blank tile. Bilal began, then stopped. Without thinking, he found himself pausing at each curve the way his uncle did, already knowing where the next leaf should go.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To describe the steps involved in making glazed tiles in Multan
choices.B: To show that Bilal's uncle is unwilling to teach him the craft
choices.C: To explain why Bilal decides to leave his uncle's workshop
choices.D: To reveal that Bilal has learned more by watching than he knew

explanation.why: Bilal complains that he is "learning nothing" because he has only mixed, swept, and watched. When his uncle hands him a brush, Bilal finds himself painting the way his uncle does, "already knowing where the next leaf should go." The passage shows that his months of watching taught him more than he realized.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Mixing glazes and painting are mentioned, but the text does not explain how tiles are made; it focuses on Bilal's discovery.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The uncle hands Bilal a brush and a tile, and Bilal's watching has already taught him, so the uncle is not refusing to teach.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Bilal complains, but the text never suggests that he decides to leave.
explanation.D: Correct. When Bilal finally paints, he moves the way his uncle does, showing that watching taught him more than he believed.
